# Upstream provenance

- Repository: https://github.com/atharva9167j/dom-to-pptx
- Imported commit: `45ee026e73b33d3fa525ebff34babbad3810d2a0`
- Imported on: 2026-07-20

## Maintained differences

- CLI entry files retain executable mode.
- pnpm permits the `esbuild` and `puppeteer` install scripts.
- The package pins pnpm 11.15.1 and supports the PPT-SDK Node.js 22 build baseline.
- Radial-gradient backgrounds are converted to SVG with deterministic solid-color fallback.
- `<img>` elements and URL background images preserve their own and inherited CSS opacity in PPTX output.
- CSS background URLs use quote-aware parsing so SVG data URLs retain internal fragment references.
- Elements with both a background color and a background image or gradient preserve the CSS layer order, with borders and shadows emitted only once.
- Rasterized images use a bounded physical-DPI budget and select JPEG only when the resulting canvas is opaque; transparent results remain PNG.
- Repeating URL textures and gradients are emitted as one tile unit with a normalizer-injected DrawingML `<a:tile>` fill instead of being stretched across the element, and the tile's `sx`/`sy` come from the raster that was actually produced rather than the requested scale.
- CSS backgrounds that an SVG gradient cannot express are painted by the browser through an SVG `<foreignObject>` rather than translated: `<stop offset>` accepts no length units (px-positioned stops collapse to offset 0 and flood the element with the first stop's colour), SVG gradients have no period for `repeating-*-gradient`, and a single `<linearGradient>`/`<radialGradient>` cannot hold a stack of layers (the greedy gradient match merged them and turned the second layer's prelude into a bogus `stop-color`, painting black). Backgrounds with a known rectangular period are painted as one tile; the rest are painted at element size. html2canvas remains a fallback but implements no `repeating-*-gradient` at all.
- `conic-gradient` counts as a gradient and is painted; it previously matched no gradient branch and no `url()`, so the whole background layer was dropped in silence.
- A stack of two or more `url()` layers is painted as one composite instead of keeping only the first layer, and never tiles — one blipFill cannot carry two periods.
- A background layer that cannot be painted logs a warning naming the element and its `background-image`; silently dropping it made a lost texture invisible until export review.
- `url()` layers are inlined as data URLs before the `<foreignObject>` painter draws them, and an element whose layers cannot all be inlined skips that painter for html2canvas. An SVG drawn through `<img>` renders in secure static mode and loads no external resource, so `linear-gradient(...), url(photo.webp)` painted the gradient and nothing else. The canvas came back non-empty, which read as success: neither the html2canvas fallback nor the lost-layer warning ran, and the photo was dropped in silence while every `<img>` on the same page exported fine.
- A whole-element background paint folds in the element's own background colour when no border or shadow sits on the base shape, so the raster is opaque and ships as JPEG instead of carrying a megabyte-scale alpha ramp. Painted rasters that turn out fully opaque on their own take the JPEG path too.
- JPEG is chosen only after inspecting the rendered pixels. Geometry that covers the canvas rules out letterboxing but not the source's own alpha, and flattening a semi-transparent texture onto JPEG black turns a faint grain into an opaque dark wash.
- PPTX media is deduplicated by content hash and all affected slide relationships are rewritten during normalization.
- Unsupported blend, mask, backdrop, and complex filter effects accept an optional managed-browser screenshot callback; standalone converter use keeps an html2canvas fallback.
- Font discovery collects every family in an element's computed CSS font stack instead of only the primary one. A stack that leads with a system CJK font and puts the web font later (`"PingFang SC", "Playfair Display", serif`) otherwise escaped auto-embed entirely.
- `@font-face` deduplication is keyed by family and PowerPoint slot rather than by URL alone. Google Fonts serves one variable-font file for several weights of a family, so URL-only dedup let the first-seen weight claim the file and left the family's other slots empty — a family could end up with `bold` and no `regular`, sending every non-bold run to a viewer substitute.
- A family whose `@font-face` declarations fill no `regular` slot has that slot backfilled from its bold, italic, or bold-italic face. CSS font matching falls back across styles within a family and PowerPoint does not: a page declaring only `Playfair Display: 700 italic` rendered fine in the browser but lost the family entirely in PowerPoint. A `regular`-only family is left alone so PowerPoint synthesises bold the way the browser does.
- Font bytes may be read through an optional `fetchFontBuffer` host hook instead of the page's `fetch`. Required for `file:` sources, which browsers refuse to `fetch`, so a font materialized on disk is unreadable from page context. Standalone use keeps browser `fetch`.
- Font embedding reports its outcome to an optional `onFontEmbedReport` callback as data. Console output alone left a headless embedder unable to tell a typography-complete export from one silently missing every web font.
- Text runs resolve an East Asian typeface separately from the Latin one and carry it through a `__ea_` typeface marker that the normalizer splits into `<a:latin>` and `<a:ea>`. PptxGenJS writes a single `fontFace` into all three script slots, which pins `<a:ea>` to a Latin font with no Han glyphs and lets PowerPoint's own substitution table pick the replacement instead of the family the CSS stack named.
- An element whose background is already painted as its own shape fill no longer repeats that background as a run `<a:highlight>`. Only a nested inline badge — one whose shape belongs to an ancestor text container — carries a highlight, and its translucent colour is flattened against the ancestor backgrounds first. PptxGenJS takes `highlight` as a bare hex, so the CSS alpha is dropped: upstream kept the highlight for every non-block element, which painted the colour a second time at full opacity. An inline-block badge styled `background: rgba(10, 69, 149, 0.08); color: #0A4595` shipped as dark blue text on an opaque dark blue slab, and the run's line-box rectangle squared off the fill's rounded corners.
- `svgToPng`/`svgToSvg` strip CSS layout properties (`position`, `left/right/top/bottom`, `inset*`, `z-index`, `float`, `clear`, `display`, `margin*`) from the serialized SVG root's inline style. They carry over from `cloneNode(true)`, mean nothing in a standalone SVG document, and make the SVG-as-image renderer offset the root out of the image viewport: a chart root styled `position:absolute; left:220px` produced a fully transparent PNG that loaded without error and embedded invisibly, so the element vanished from the deck in silence (preset-111 p6 line chart, p9 timeline arrows, and every absolutely-positioned inline-styled SVG with a non-zero offset). Width/height, transform, and paint properties are kept.
- A paragraph's exact line spacing (`<a:lnSpc>`) is the tallest line box in the paragraph — the maximum across its runs plus the strut of the block that owns the line — rather than whatever the surviving `<a:pPr>` happened to carry. A `line-height` written as a bare number re-resolves against each element's own font-size, so `1860<span style="font-size: 32px">万</span>` under `font-size: 88px; line-height: 0.9` asked for 39.6pt on the number and 14.4pt on the unit. PptxGenJS emits one `<a:pPr>` per run and only one survives, so the unit span sized the whole line; exact spacing is laid out from the line bottom, which pushed the digits up out of their frame and into the label above. The normalizer keeps the largest of duplicate exact `<a:lnSpc>` values for the same reason, and leaves mixed `spcPct`/`spcPts` duplicates — which share no scale to compare on — on the previous keep-the-last behaviour.

Upstream changes are reviewed and selectively ported into this directory. Do not replace this directory from an external checkout wholesale.
